title: Integrations
intro: Use PulseStage from inside Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP-compatible assistants. Attach your presentation slides in the chat and ask for questions: the assistant creates the session and places each interaction after the right slide.
notReady: Assistant connections aren't active on this server yet. Whoever runs PulseStage needs to turn on the OAuth server in Supabase (see the README).

server.title: MCP server address
server.description: It's the same for every assistant. The first time, it opens PulseStage so you can sign in and allow access.

connect.title: Connect
connect.description: Menu names may vary a little depending on each app's version.
connect.allowStep: Sign in with your PulseStage account and click Allow access.

claude.step1: In Claude (web or app), open Settings → Connectors and click Add custom connector.
claude.step2: Name: PulseStage. URL: the address above. Save and click Connect.
claude.step4: In a chat, turn on PulseStage in the tools menu and attach your presentation PDF.

chatgpt.step1: In ChatGPT, open Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings and turn on Developer mode (custom connectors depend on your plan).
chatgpt.step2: In Apps & Connectors, click Create. Name: PulseStage; MCP server URL: the address above; authentication: OAuth.
chatgpt.step4: In a chat, pick PulseStage from the “+” menu and attach your presentation PDF.

code.after: Then, inside Claude Code, run /mcp, choose pulsestage and authenticate in your browser.

others.text: Any MCP client with remote (HTTP) servers and OAuth sign-in works, like Cursor and VS Code: add a server with the address above. The client figures out where to sign in on its own.

usage.title: Using it with a finished presentation
usage.description: The assistant reads the slides in the chat; PulseStage only receives the questions.
usage.step1: Attach your presentation PDF to the chat and mention the audience and the length.
usage.step2: The assistant suggests the questions and which slide each one comes after (using the PDF page numbers). Tweak anything you like and approve.
usage.step3: It creates the session (or uses one you point to) and saves the questions in the right place.
usage.step4: Open the session in PulseStage, go to the “Slides” tab and upload the same PDF: the questions already show up between the slides. You can drag and edit them as usual.
usage.note: The assistant doesn't start or end the live session: that still happens in PulseStage. Ended sessions can't be edited, but it can read the results to review the presentation with you.

fromSlides.title: From your slides
fromSlides.text: I've attached my presentation. Use PulseStage to plan 5 interactions for this 50-minute talk for high school teachers. Show me the plan before creating anything.

fromScratch.title: A class from scratch
fromScratch.text: In PulseStage, create the session “Fractions – 6th grade” for tomorrow at 10 a.m., with a word cloud to kick things off and a 4-question quiz with a 20-second timer.

adjust.title: Adjust the lineup
adjust.text: In my session “Leading remote teams”, replace the question after slide 8 with a harder quiz and move the scale to the end.

afterTalk.title: After the talk
afterTalk.text: Analyze the results of my latest PulseStage session: what worked, where the audience struggled most and what to change next time.

connected.title: Connected assistants
connected.description: Each one acts as you, with access to your sessions. Revoke the ones you no longer use. Details in <link>Privacy</link>.

connectedApps.emptyDescription: When you connect Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant, it shows up here.
connectedApps.revokeDescription: The assistant immediately stops seeing and editing your sessions. To use it again, connect it again.

consent.expired: The connection request has expired or was already used.
consent.tryAgain: Go back to the assistant (Claude, ChatGPT or another) and ask it to connect PulseStage again.
consent.title: {client} wants to access your account
consent.actsAs: It will act as {email} and then return to {host}.
consent.canTitle: Through PulseStage's tools, it will be able to:

can.read: See your sessions, lineups and their results (votes, averages, open-ended answers and survey comments)
can.write: Create sessions and create, edit, move and delete questions

consent.cannotTitle: The tools don't allow it to:

cannot.personal: See names, emails or phone numbers of the people who took part
cannot.live: Start, pause or end a live session
cannot.account: Delete sessions or change your account

consent.warning: Only allow this if you just asked for it and you trust this app: it gets access to your account. You can revoke it anytime under Integrations in your dashboard.
consent.notYou: Not you? <switch>Sign in with another account</switch>
